findings.title: website_name leaks the website of TL0 users whose profile fields are hidden from anonymous visitors
findings.body: This serializer deliberately hides `website` (along with bio/location/etc.) for trust-level-0 users viewed by logged-out visitors, via `untrusted_attributes`, which defines `include_website?` to return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. The new `website_name` attribute (declared at line 43) is not in the untrusted list and its include guard only checks `website.present?`, so for a TL0 spammer the JSON still contains `website_name` with the host/path of the website even though `website` itself is omitted — and the profile template renders that name next to the globe icon. This defeats the anti-spam measure that hides new users' links from anonymous viewers. Fix by adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (or honoring `scope.restrict_user_fields?` in its include check) and add a spec covering an anonymous view of a TL0 user with a website.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix, so ActiveModelSerializers never calls it
findings.body: ActiveModelSerializers decides whether to emit an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?`. Every other guard in this file follows that convention (`include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_card_badge?`, etc.), but the new method is defined as `include_website_name` without the question mark. It is therefore never invoked, and `website_name` is always serialized — including `"website_name": null` for users who have no website set. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: Same-length host comparison treats unrelated domains on a shared suffix as the same site
findings.body: The `elsif` branch drops the first dot-separated label of both the website host and the instance host and compares the remainders whenever both hosts have the same number of labels (> 2). That works for the intended `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` case, but it also matches completely unrelated sites that share a parent or public suffix: e.g. website `example.co.uk` with instance `another.co.uk` compares `co.uk == co.uk`, and `alice.github.io` vs `bob.github.io` compares `github.io == github.io`, causing the profile to display the full URL path of an unrelated website. Compare registrable domains (e.g. via PublicSuffix) instead of blindly stripping the first label.

findings.title: website_name is stale after the user edits their website
findings.body: Previously the displayed label was a computed property (`websiteName`) derived from `model.website`, so editing the website in preferences updated the profile display immediately. Now the label comes from the server as `website_name`, and the `save()` success handler only applies `bio_excerpt` from the PUT response, discarding the recomputed `website_name` even though the server returns it. After changing their website, the user keeps seeing the old label on their profile until a full page reload. Apply `data.user.website_name` (and ideally `website`) from the save response, or refetch the user.
